items.q: When do "mate value" market forces actually dominate?
items.a: Mostly at **first contact** (forehead-number demo). With time together, consensus ratings dissolve into **idiosyncratic compatibility** — "everyone thinks you're a five, but she thinks you're a ten."

items.q: Is instant 10/10 chemistry how most relationships start?
items.a: No — the **typical first impression is middling**. Desire often builds via **slow accumulation** of shared moments and "with me, he seems…" stories, not checkbox traits.

items.q: What's wrong with swipe markets for lasting bonds?
items.a: They amplify **inequality** (popular people hoard swipes) and select for **looks and witty texting** that don't predict lasting bonds — among the **most unequal markets** claimed in the world.

items.q: Where should you meet people instead?
items.a: Prefer **repeated exposure in small groups** — church, improv, sports, couple friends, recurring beach volleyball or cooking nights. Young adults socialize less; tech pulls away from the architecture we evolved for.

items.q: Do deep questions beat hotness-alone small talk?
items.a: Yes — **Fast Friends / 36 questions** elicit reciprocal self-disclosure. Being truly heard often beats trait-checklist banter; humans bond through **shared narratives**, not surveys.

items.q: Does actual similarity predict whether you'll click?
items.a: **Perceived similarity** beats actual similarity. On real traits you're often **no better than a coin flip** at predicting a click. Face-to-face, trust "I'm not feeling this" over consensus filters.

items.q: Do men and women want totally different partners face-to-face?
items.a: Stated survey gaps largely **collapse** with real people — including preferences for **younger partners** and ambition/finances. Eastwick pushes back on **heteropessimism** and junior-high internet narratives.

items.q: Who is more eager to commit on average?
items.a: **Men** are slightly more eager — more likely to say **"I love you" first** and want exclusivity; women are more likely to want to break up, partly because they cultivate broader **couple-friends support** while men lean harder on the partner.

items.q: Which intimacy signal predicts relationship satisfaction?
items.a: Rating your partner as a **"good lover"** is among the **strongest predictors** of how positively you feel about the relationship — subjective sexual fit matters a lot.

items.q: How do happy couples protect monogamy day to day?
items.a: They feel the partner is **uniquely irreplaceable** and use **derogation of alternatives** (downrating attractive others). Secretive escalation (e.g. Instagram DMs) erodes that layer more than fleeting attraction alone.
